[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/4: [agency] "He cries to the only one who can give light" vs "πρὸς τὸν μόνον φωτίσαι δυνάμενον": Subject is 'man' needing crying-out; no 'he cries to' in source, just 'toward the only one able to light'; [modality] "who can bring about a change from these evils" vs "καὶ τῶν κακῶν ἐργάσασθαι μεταβολήν": Infinitive 'to work/accomplish a change of the evils', not 'from these evils'; [completeness] "twisting it to suit their own will" vs "κατὰ τὸ ἑαυτῶν βούλημα διασύροντες": Missing 'dragging through/reviling' (διασύροντες); 'twisting' too weak; [agency] "with a rock pushing through and dislodging their rooting" vs "διὰ πέτρας ὠθούσης καὶ τὴν ῥίζωσιν ἐκτοπούσης": Rock is subject of both participles; 'their rooting' obscures that rock dislodges the rooting; [negation] "mocking what is holy" vs "τὰ σεμνὰ γελῶντες": τὰ σεμνὰ = 'the reverend/seemly things', not specifically 'holy'; contrast is with τὰ ἀσεμνὰ; [completeness] "because they delight in what is unholy" vs "διὰ τὸ τοῖς ἀσέμνοις χαίρειν": Missing 'by-long habit' (χρονίᾳ τῇ περὶ ταῦτα συνηθείᾳ) as second cause; merged into one clause; [scripture] "Ps 140,4.5; Ps 140,6.7" vs "292 Ps 140,4.5; 293 Ps 140,6.7": LXX Ps 140 = Hebrew/English Ps 141; should be Ps 141[140] | part 2/4: [source_identity] "Second, he speaks of the sorrow of death" vs "δεύτερον τὸ περὶ τοῦ θανάτου λέγει τὸ λυπηρόν": τὸ λυπηρόν modifies dissolution, not death; 'sorrow of death' misattributes grief; [agency] "like a clod of earth breaking apart, he is scattered" vs "βώλου τρόπῳ διαλυομένου σκεδάννυται": dative of manner 'in manner of clod' not 'like'; passive 'is scattered' obscures middle force; [modality] "'Let the lawless fall'" vs "Ἐμπέσοιεν": optative of wish 'may they fall' not jussive 'let them fall'; [completeness] "Let their schemes, he says, turn against them" vs "εἰς αὐτούς, φησί, περισταίη μηχανήματα": adds 'their schemes' for μηχανήματα; no possessive in source; [negation] "not to come near them or be entangled with them" vs "τὸ μηδὲ πλησιάζειν μηδὲ συμφύρεσθαι": μηδέ...μηδέ is 'neither...nor' not 'not...or'; alters logical structure; [scripture] "(Lamentations 3:27-28)" vs "Ἱερεμίας": source cites Jeremiah, not Lamentations; editorial bracket contradicts source attribution; [modality] "since we would have to go out of the world" vs "ἐπεὶ ὀφείλομεν ἄρα ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελθεῖν": ὀφείλομεν is 'we ought/debt' not 'would have to'; ἄρα 'then/inferentially' dropped | part 3/4: [agency] "when it places the Lord and God in such a relation" vs "ἐπὶ τοιούτου τιθεῖσα τὸν κύριον καὶ τὸν θεόν": Missing subject: the unity places them, not 'it' impersonally; 'in such a relation' obscures ἐπὶ τοιούτου; [completeness] "In this way the properties of the divine and lordly essence" vs "Missing 'according to which' (καθὸ); 'properties' adds interpretation not in source": None; [agency] "proceeding from the Father to the Son" vs "ἐκ πατρὸς μὲν εἰς υἱὸν ὁρμηθέντα": ὁρμηθέντα is passive/middle 'having rushed/impelled,' not active 'proceeding'; [agency] "and led back from the Son to God" vs "ἐξ υἱοῦ δὲ εἰς θεὸν ἀναγόμενα": ἀναγόμενα is passive 'being led back,' but subject is the properties/essence, not an agent; [modality] "He does not set as the goal" vs "Οὐ τῷ φυγεῖν δὲ...τίθεται τέλος": Subject is unclear in Greek; 'He' is supplied, but could be the psalmist/David; τίθεται is passive 'is set'; [scripture] "Ps 141,2" vs "Ps 141,2": Correct LXX numbering; Hebrew/English would be Psalm 142:1-2; [scripture] "Ps 141,8" vs "Ps 141,8": Correct LXX numbering; Hebrew/English would be Psalm 142:7; [scripture] "Ps 142 arg." vs "Ps 142 arg.": Correct LXX numbering; Hebrew/English would be Psalm 143 title/argument; [negation] "not without a title" vs "μὴ εἶναι ἀνεπίγραφον": Correctly rendered double negative, but 'without a title' for ἀνεπίγραφον is acceptable; [completeness] "'A Psalm of David, when his son pursued him.'" vs "Ψαλμὸς τῷ ∆αυίδ, ὅτε αὐτὸν ὁ υἱὸς κατεδίωκεν": Missing 'to David' (τῷ ∆αυίδ dative), translated as 'of David' | part 4/4: [agency] "he does not yet receive the perfect mercy now" vs "ἢ τὸν τέλεον ἔλεον οὔπω νῦν ἐπιδέχεται": Subject is 'the righteous' (τῶν δικαίων), not 'he'; generic plural, not individual.; [modality] "he does not yet receive" vs "ἐπιδέχεται": ἐπιδέχεται means 'receives/accepts/welcomes,' not negative; 'does not yet receive' misrepresents.; [agency] "but awaits the future appearing" vs "ἀλλὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπιφάνειαν": No verb 'awaits' in source; participle or implied continuation, not active waiting.; [completeness] "when the Master will shine upon the righteous" vs "ὅτε καταυγάσει δικαίους ὁ δεσπότης": δικαίους is accusative object of shining upon, not subject; 'the righteous' are recipients, not agents.; [agency] "He asks that the name of goodness become for him" vs "Τὸ τῆς ἀγαθότητος ὄνομα... πρόφασιν ἑαυτῷ γίνεσθαι ἀξιοῖ": Subject is again generic 'the righteous' from context, not 'he'; ἀξιοῖ is third person.; [scripture] "(Ephesians 1:6)" vs "Εἰς ἔπαινον τῆς δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ": Verse is Ephesians 1:6 in NA28/UBS, but LXX Psalm citation context may affect numbering; however this is correct.
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/4: [source_identity] "They mock what is good, he says, and disparage what is by common agreement the most beautiful thing of all" vs "Ὅτι, φησί, χλευάζουσι τὸ καλὸν καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ ὁμολογουμένως κάλλιστον": τὸ καλόν is singular 'the beautiful/good thing,' not 'what is good'; one object mocked, not two.; [source_identity] "mocking what is holy because they delight in what is unholy" vs "τὰ σεμνὰ γελῶντες διὰ τὸ τοῖς ἀσέμνοις χαίρειν": ἀσέμνοις means 'unseemly/shameful,' not 'unholy'; σεμνά means 'solemn/venerable,' not strictly 'holy.'; [source_identity] "asking for what is good and truly lovely and delightful" vs "τὴν αἴτησιν ἐκκεκόφθαι τὴν περὶ τὰ καλὰ καὶ ὄντως ποθεινὰ καὶ τερπνά": καλά is plural 'beautiful/good things,' not singular 'what is good'; ποθεινά means 'desirable,' not 'lovely.' | part 2/4: [scripture] "'It is good for a man when he bears the yoke in his youth; he will sit alone and be silent' (Lamentations 3:27-28)" vs "Ἀγαθὸν ἀνδρὶ ὅταν ἄρῃ ζυγὸν ἐν νεότητι αὐτοῦ· καθήσεται κατὰ μόνας καὶ σιωπήσεται": Source cites Jeremiah; English adds parenthetical Lamentations 3:27-28 not in the Greek source text.
Latin quote (from model note, verified): «πρὸς τὸν μόνον φωτίσαι δυνάμενον»
English quote (from model note, verified): «He cries to the only one who can give light»
ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. The revised 'Or, according to the whole theme …' now reflects ἢ. The verb ἐπιδέχεται is negated by οὔπω ('he does not yet receive'), and 'awaits' supplies the verb for the second object, τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπιφάνειαν. Lamentations 3:27-28 correctly identifies the quoted Ἀγαθὸν ἀνδρὶ ὅταν ἄρῃ ζυγὸν …, traditionally ascribed to Jeremiah as the Greek does. 'Ps 140,4.5', 'Ps 141,2' etc. are edition lemmata. Optative 'let' for Ἐμπέσοιεν, 'twisting' for διασύροντες, 'holy/unholy' for σεμνά/ἄσεμνα and supplied subjects are idiom.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. 'What is good' for τὸ καλόν and 'unholy' for τοῖς ἀσέμνοις render the contrast with the same sense, and 'lovely' for ποθεινά is acceptable. Lamentations 3:27-28 is the correct modern reference for the words the Greek attributes to Jeremiah.
